The Parliament of Scotland ( Scots : Pairlament o Scotland ; Scottish Gaelic : Pàrlamaid na h-Alba ), also known as the Estates of Scotland , [ 4 ] was the legislature of the Kingdom of Scotland from the 13th century until 1707. The parliament evolved during the early 13th century from the king's council of bishops and earls , with the first identifiable parliament being held in 1235 during the reign of Alexander II , when it already possessed a political and judicial role.
